No compiler CFG, arbitrary virtual dispatch, alias analysis or full-program authorization proof. Macros are expanded only from the scan's own sources and only when unambiguous; the catalogue is never an #include resolution, and what the expander refused is counted in the macro-expansion limitation rather than assumed away.
Unmodeled callees/authorization remain evidence obligations; no findings does not establish safety.

Interface-descriptor identity is read from the class's own base clause: a comparison is counted as this transaction's guard only when the source names the interface the class implements. A comparison against another interface, or one whose identity the analysed sources do not state, is reported with that reason instead of counting as a guard or as a proven mismatch.
Descriptor consistency is separate from caller authorization; relay candidates are not exploit proofs.

IPC roots require a source-indexed class dispatcher with code, request Parcel and reply Parcel; explicit service/transport roots and Stub inner helpers are separate allowlisted entry kinds. Test/fuzz/mock path roots are excluded from product candidate analysis and counted in limitations. Entry discovery is not reachability: dispatcher-level guards and macro-conditional reachability remain obligations, not conclusions.
Entry-coverage measurements are published in the interface research report, not in this result.

Cross-service boundary coverage: 0 call(s) on a handle built by iface_cast<> in the scanned sources, 0 carrying the original caller's identity (SetCallingIdentity with a calling-token value active), 0 executing as the service. Each boundary is recorded with the identity that crossed it; no candidate is emitted from the boundary itself, and a downstream service's own guards are not read from this corpus.

Entry/dispatch coverage: 0 dispatcher(s) (0 in stub classes, 0 with a recognizable guard before dispatch), 0 binding(s) by grade {}, transactions {}, unresolved dispatch {}, 0 binding(s) under a preprocessor condition. A binding is not reachability; a refused binding is unknown, not safe.
